preamble: Depalatalization of the palatalized lateral [lʲ] to the plain alveolar lateral [l] is a phonological process documented both diachronically in language change and synchronically in contemporary variation. This process commonly occurs in language contact situations, phonotactic restrictions, and historical sound shifts across Slavic and Uralic languages.

examples.note: In the evolution of Czech from Common Slavic (10th–11th centuries), palatalized [lʲ] lost its palatalization, diverging from East Slavic languages like Russian which retained the contrast.
In western dialects /ʎ/ lost its palatal feature and merged with /l/; northern dialects keep it.
